sentiment: Nobody knows the body's arithmetic. What holds is a small room, a warm lamp, and attention that doesn't flinch.

stories.title: Things to know when you get cancer
stories.summary: A patient writes down what the doctors didn't say plainly — the practical tenderness that only arrives once the news is real.

stories.title: Do dentists know what they're doing?
stories.summary: Even the experts are working from training and habit, not certainty — which is oddly reassuring about the rest of us.

stories.title: Tiny Little Office
stories.summary: A small room with one purpose and one lamp, and somehow that is the whole argument for how a person should work.
